title: Crescent rollout notes and shift compose — Jun 2027 (draft)
body:
SUMMARY:
A compact rollout plan for the 'Crescent' traffic-shaping change and a handover template were calling 'Shift Compose' (a short form for shift composition/companion notes). This doc is intentionally terse: operational checklist, 72-hour calendar, quick-release notes draft, and a short list of fallout/rollback triggers.

SCOPE:
- Deploy: traffic-shaping + safe-throttle on model-routing service (router v2.3)
- Affects: hosted-api route /v1/generate, dedicated pools in us-west-2; not touching private deployments
- Goal: reduce tail latency tail events during bursty traffic windows by ~20% via progressive throttles and prefix-caching tuning

OBJECTIVES (what success looks like):
- 99th percentile latency improves by >= 15% within 2 hours after full rollout
- Error budget consumption for /v1/generate remains <= 10% of daily allowance during rollforward
- No customer-facing errors > P2; any P1 auto-rollback

CRESCENT ROLLOUT CALENDAR (72h window)
- Day -2 (2027-06-13): dry-run in staging; smoke tests + burst sim (team: se-sim)
- Day -1 (2027-06-14): canary in us-west-2, 0.5% traffic for 30m, observe; shift compose handoffs prepared
- Day 0 (2027-06-15): micro-increment rollout schedule (see increments below)
  - 09:00 UTC: increase to 2% for 1h (monitoring tag: crescent-canary-1)
  - 11:30 UTC: if green, 10% for 2h (crescent-canary-2)
  - 14:00 UTC: 25% for 3h (crescent-wave-1)
  - 18:00 UTC: 50% for 2h (crescent-wave-2)
  - 21:00 UTC: 100% (full) if all gates pass
- Day +1 (2027-06-16): stability watch; rollback cutoff at 02:00 UTC if error budget exceeded
- Day +2 (2027-06-17): post-rollout validation and rollout retro

SHIFT COMPOSE (handovers and narrative)
- Lead on-call (09:00–17:00): Marcus Li (eng-release-eng)
- Night on-call (17:00–01:00): Sofia Ramirez (sre)
- Overnight anchor (01:00–09:00): Ethan Gold (serving-runtime)
- Handoff template (to paste in Slack #release-ops):
  - "State: crescent-wave-X at Y%"
  - Active alarms and top 3 alerts (include links)
  - Key telemetry snapshot (latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate)
  - Any mitigation actions taken (what, why, who)

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (must be green before Day -1 canary)
- [ ] Staging dry-run completed (artifact: REL-4821)
- [ ] Loadtest with 2x expected peak (se-sim signoff)
- [ ] Rollback playbook baked and smoke scripts validated
- [ ] Observability: dashboards created, pager shortcuts prefilled (obs ID: dash/crescent-watch)
- [ ] Communications: customer incident template loaded; CS notified of potential minor degradation

INCREMENTAL ROLLOUT STEPS (operator playbook)
- Step 0: set throttle to baseline; add deployment tag crescent:pre
- Step 1: push router v2.3 to a small cohort; enable prefix-caching false-positive guardrails
- Step 2: apply safe-throttle at 0.5% traffic; mark monitoring tag crescent-canary-1
- Step 3: wait 30m, check p50/p95/p99 and error budget. If p99 spike > +30% baseline or errors increase > 0.2% absolute -> rollback to previous routing policy and escalate
- Step 4: if green, continue to next increment per calendar times

ROLLBACK TRIGGERS (automated/manual)
- Automated: any sustained 5m window where error-rate > 1.5x baseline AND p99 > 2x baseline -> automatic rollback to previous routing set
- Manual: any P1 incident, or sustained customer impact reported by CS (ticket severity >= Sev2)
- On rollback: communicate in #release-ops, run postmortem checklist, pause rollout for 24h

TELEMETRY & SIGNALS (what to watch)
- Primary: p99 latency (route=/v1/generate), 5m windows, sampled across regions
- Secondary: error-rate (4xx/5xx), throughput, request queue depth on router instances
- Canary-only: sampling of top 50 slow traces to Sentry (tag: crescent-canary)

QUICK RELEASE NOTES (draft to ship with rollout)
- Title: router: safer throttles + prefix cache tuning (router v2.3)
- Summary: Incremental rollout of routing improvements that reduce tail latency under burst. No changes to API surface.
- Notable changes: safe-throttle policy added to router; prefix caching heuristics adjusted to keep KV cache warm under short sessions.
- Impact: expected improvement in 99th percentile latency for chat/generation use-cases; tiny risk of transient 429s during initial ramp (mitigated by roll-forward rules).
- Rollback: automatic rollback and manual abort criteria documented; contact eng-release-engineering oncall for unresolved issues.

KNOWN RISKS & MITIGATIONS
- Risk: 429 storm if throttle misparameterized -> mitigation: cap ramp rate and immediate automated rollback on error spike
- Risk: cache thrash in long-running sessions -> mitigation: enable session-scoped hints and reduce cache eviction margin for 48h post-rollout
- Unknown: interplay with Dedicated autoscaling; SRE to watch pool saturation metrics

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs
- Q1: confirm whether private-deploy customers who mirror hosted configs will receive advisory notice. Owner: Marcus (ACTION)
- Q2: do we need an extra sim that includes sustained low-qps long sessions? Owner: se-sim (ACTION)
- TODO: link final runbook to the deploy ticket and pin in #release-ops (Aisha)

POST-ROLL & RETRO AGENDA (Day +2)
- 09:00 UTC: signal review (p50/p95/p99) and followup ticket triage
- 10:00 UTC: short retro (30m): what worked, what broke, action items
- Deliverables: small PRs for improved observability added to REL-4821; followups assigned in the sprint backlog

NOTES TO SELF (rough fragments)
- Keep comm short: customers care about errors > 0.25% or persistent latency regressions.
- If we do partial rollback, try to freeze routing policy and open a small experiment lane to test alternate throttle curve.
- Remember: consolidate Sentry slow-trace examples into a single doc for postmortem (helps SRE triage)

CONTACTS
- Release lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Oncall channel: #release-ops (primary), #sre-alerts (escalation)
- Runbook ticket: https://jira.redwoodinfra/browse/REL-4821

END — keep this doc as the quick operational slate; final runbook to be produced if we promote after Day +2 retro."
